notes: SHIP v1.14.415 - SINGLE-MASTER LAW: PHANTOM NOW HAS EXACTLY ONE AUTHORITATIVE MASTER, AND ONE DOOR THAT WRITES IT. Owner ruling of 2026-08-08: there must never be one Master in memory and another in storage, one driving Build and another driving Forge, or a candidate that half-becomes active. An audit of every place a Master lives found SIX ways the code could disagree with itself, ALL reachable, and this ship closes all six. Two commits, one stamp. WHERE A MASTER LIVED BEFORE THIS SHIP: the live global window._lastPhantomMaster (4 writers, ~35 readers), the phantom_master_v1 snapshot (1 writer, 4 readers), the Forge _slotCache (no identity, no invalidation), _mscopeState.siteRef (a captured reference PREFERRED over the global), the EDP cache (keyed with masterHash - the only one that carried identity), and the jobsnap (a deliberate snapshot, spec'd never to read the live Master - legitimate, untouched). THE CONTRACT. New PHANTOM_MASTER owns both halves of active: the live pointer and the persisted snapshot. ORDERING IS THE WHOLE MECHANISM - replace() persists FIRST and goes live SECOND, so a candidate that cannot be persisted never becomes active and the two cannot diverge. That single inversion closes defects 1 and 2 by construction rather than by remembering to check. The global stays the live pointer by choice: 35 readers already use it and rewriting them all is a far larger blast radius than the defect. What changed is that it may only be WRITTEN in one place - verified, the only assignments left in the file are the contract's own. DEFECT 1 - v1.14.414's OWN OVERWRITE GUARD CREATED SPLIT-BRAIN BY DESIGN. When save() refused a host-less Master, the caller assigned the candidate to the live global anyway. I shipped that two days ago and described it as costing nothing in-session; under this ruling it is the textbook forbidden state - memory holding the candidate, storage holding the previous Master, every surface reading whichever half it happened to consult. This ship is the correction. DEFECT 2 - v1.14.406's quota path had the identical shape: save() returns false, candidate goes live regardless. Same fix, same line of reasoning. DEFECT 3 - RECONCILE RAN ON A DIFFERENT MASTER THAN THE REST OF THE APP. reconcile_run read the persisted store ONLY and never looked at the live Master - the one consumer in the app that did. With memory holding B and storage holding A it produced its answer from A while Build and Forge worked on B, simultaneously and with equal confidence. It now reads the active Master through the contract. Its cache key was the same disease in a second place: the Master term was sourceFileHash with NO stats fallback, and a freshly parsed Master carries that hash at stats.sourceFileHash, so on a fresh import the term silently degraded to empty and TWO DIFFERENT MASTERS PRODUCED THE SAME KEY - Reconcile serving Master A's stored result under Master B. idOf() is now the single definition of Master identity and absorbs both shapes. DEFECT 4 - THE FORGE SLOT CACHE COULD OUTLIVE ITS MASTER. _slotCache carried no Master identity and had no invalidation, so slots computed under Master A were returned while B was active. Worse, the hit test was a bare truthiness check, so an EMPTY array counted as a hit: a rack read once while the Master was unusable stayed empty for the life of the page. The cache is now stamped with the Master id and checked on every read - self-healing, and it cannot be defeated by forgetting to call an invalidator. A registered listener clears it too; the stamp alone is sufficient, and it is what makes this correct under a replace that lands between two reads. DEFECT 5 - A SECOND ACTIVE POINTER. _mscopeState.siteRef was a captured reference consulted BEFORE the live Master, which meant a scope staged against Master A could be committed against A after B had replaced it. The active Master is now authoritative and siteRef is honoured only while it still refers to the same Master identity. DEFECT 6 - THE PARSER PERSISTED BEFORE ANYTHING JUDGED THE CANDIDATE. phantom_parseMaster wrote the parse result straight to storage - a writer outside the contract, firing at parse time. Parsing Master B while A was active put B in storage and left A live: the forbidden state, reached with no caller intending to switch Masters, and it survived a reload as B. PARSE IS NOW PURE - it returns a candidate and changes nothing. Persistence did not go away, it moved to the one door, which still saves before going live, so cold-start hydration is unchanged for every Master an operator actually adopts. Only the ones nobody adopted stop being written. THE ONE EXCEPTION, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. If persistence fails and there is NO prior Master, the candidate is accepted live with storage guaranteed EMPTY. That is not split-brain - nothing disagrees, there is simply no persisted Master - and the alternative is refusing to let an operator use a Master at all on a device whose quota the file exceeds. It is flagged unpersisted so any surface can say so, and it dies at restart honestly. When a prior Master DOES exist, a failed candidate is rejected outright and the prior one stays active in BOTH places: never destroy known-good data for a candidate that cannot be kept. A refused import now toasts to say the existing Master is still active, rather than failing quietly. OPERATOR-VISIBLE CHANGES: a Master that cannot be persisted while another is active is REFUSED and says so, instead of going half-live. A purge now drops the live pointer, the snapshot and every Master-derived cache in one call, so it cannot leave a stale Forge slot cache behind. Everything else is invariant work with no surface change. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces balanced, CRLF intact on dct-ios.html with 0 lone LF, three-stamp lockstep, full Playwright regression green. No UI surface changed, no RACK SCENE LOCK term touched, ?legacy=1 unaffected - the contract is house-agnostic because a data invariant is never house-scoped. DEVICE-VERIFY: clear the service-worker cache and confirm v1.14.415. Then the one thing worth your hands: load your real Master, confirm the cab count is what it has always been, open Forge and confirm a populated rack still resolves its devices. Then re-load the SAME Master a second time and confirm nothing changes and nothing is lost - that is the replace path running end to end. phantom_clearMaster() in the console remains the escape.
